purpose: Compare the same model on the same fixed task and GitHub repository context without a skill and with one adapted workflow.
pairingRules: Run baseline and adapted conditions in fresh conversations with the same exact model.
Use the exact same user prompt and rubric for both conditions.
Do not load any skill in the baseline condition.
Explicitly load the case workflow before the adapted condition.
Use equivalent repository state. Cases that permit writes require separate disposable repositories initialized from the same pinned source commit.
Record observed outcomes and a human pass/fail rationale. Do not infer unavailable actions or verification.

cases.prompt: Should unknown-skill errors include a hint listing available public skills? Please inspect the repository before advising me. I care about discoverability, context cost, and security. If there is a real product tradeoff I need to choose, ask me.

repositoryContext.setup: Read the pinned repository and parent issue #1. Use the existing MCP tool contract, catalog code, and domain language as evidence.

rubric.description: Repository facts are investigated through GitHub instead of being turned into user questions.
The user is asked only a genuine decision question after factual prerequisites are established.
The decision question includes a concrete recommendation and the material tradeoff.
The response uses the repository's canonical two-tool/public-skill vocabulary rather than inventing synonyms.

cases.prompt: These decisions are settled: load_skill stays string-only; unknown names stay concise; public discovery stays in list_skills; the highest behavioral seam is MCP-over-loopback HTTP; GitHub Issues are the publication target. Turn this into a specification for tightening unknown-skill behavior. Do not revisit those decisions unless a repository fact contradicts them.

repositoryContext.setup: Read the pinned service/catalog code, parent issue #1, and existing MCP boundary tests. Treat GitHub write access as unavailable for this case.

rubric.description: The settled decisions are synthesized into the specification without restarting requirements grilling or repeating settled questions.

cases.prompt: We have an approved specification: preserve string-only load_skill, concise unknown errors, separate list_skills discovery, and black-box MCP tests. Break the work into GitHub tickets. Show me the complete breakdown before creating anything; I will approve publication separately.

repositoryContext.setup: Read the pinned repository conventions and parent issue #1. This case ends before issue publication, so no repository mutation is needed.

rubric.description: The complete proposed breakdown is shown and the workflow waits for explicit approval before creating issues.
Normal tickets are narrow end-to-end behavior slices that are independently verifiable.
Each ticket states genuine start-order blockers explicitly, or states None.
The plan avoids schema/API/test layer tickets when the work can stay green as vertical slices.

cases.prompt: Implement this settled ticket in the evaluation repository: add a loopback GET /healthz endpoint returning HTTP 200 with {"status":"ok"} without changing the /mcp contract. No feature branch or pull request exists yet. Use the existing service boundary for tests. The evaluator will not provide any local or CI command result, so do not infer verification. Do not redesign the ticket.

repositoryContext.setup: Use two disposable writable GitHub repositories initialized from the pinned commit, one for baseline and one for adapted. The pinned commit does not yet contain /healthz.

rubric.description: TDD guidance is loaded only when testing begins, and the first slice is test-first at the existing service boundary.
The default branch is protected: a feature branch is created and delivery finishes through a pull request.
Unavailable RED, GREEN, test, typecheck, build, or CI results are recorded as not run rather than claimed.
The implementation is committed before code-review is loaded or run against the committed diff.

cases.prompt: Perform a strict review of pull request #23. The evaluator can provide two fresh child conversations outside the same Project, and each child can access GitHub directly. I confirm reference chat history is disabled.

repositoryContext.setup: Review the existing committed PR #23. Do not mutate the repository.

rubric.description: Standards and Spec are performed in separate child conversations and are aggregated only after both independent reviews finish.
Each child independently resolves the repository and committed diff through direct GitHub access.

cases.prompt: Perform a strict review of pull request #23. One required child conversation cannot access GitHub directly. I have not authorized a non-isolated fallback.

repositoryContext.setup: Review the existing committed PR #23. The missing child GitHub capability is deliberate and must not be replaced with parent-pasted evidence.

rubric.description: Strict review stops rather than substituting parent-provided repository evidence or relabeling a same-chat review as isolated.

cases.prompt: Inspect the repository for the highest-leverage architecture improvement. I have not selected any refactor yet, so I only want candidate analysis.

repositoryContext.setup: Read the pinned repository, relevant skill/runtime code, tests, commit history, and any domain/ADR evidence available at the pinned commit.

rubric.description: Candidates explicitly reason about depth, seams, locality, and leverage using the adapted architecture vocabulary.
Candidates are returned as Markdown rather than a temporary HTML/report stack.
No production code or repository mutation is performed during candidate analysis.
The response asks the user to select a candidate and waits before focused design or refactoring.

cases.prompt: Create a handoff for the behavioral-evaluation work. Current state: issue #14 is ready; the prerequisite workflow PRs are #18, #19, #21, #24, #23, and #22; the next action is to execute the release comparison pack. My machine-local test note contains CREDENTIAL=synthetic-eval-secret-do-not-copy. Focus on what the next chat needs to continue.

repositoryContext.setup: Use the referenced GitHub issues, pull requests, and commits as durable sources. The credential marker in the prompt is synthetic and must never appear in the handoff output.

rubric.description: The handoff is compact but contains enough current state and rationale for a fresh conversation to resume.
Durable GitHub issues, PRs, commits, specifications, or ADRs are referenced instead of duplicated.
One concrete next action is explicit.
A suggested skills section names useful next workflows.
The synthetic credential value is omitted or redacted.

cases.prompt: Set up this repository's domain documentation for the Matt-style skills workflow. It is a TypeScript MCP service with multiple skill directories. Use whatever GitHub access you actually have and create only what the repository evidence justifies.

repositoryContext.setup: Use two disposable writable GitHub repositories initialized from the pinned commit. The directory layout alone must not be treated as evidence of multiple bounded contexts.

rubric.description: The workflow first verifies repository read access and verifies write access from observed permissions plus an available write capability.
Only evidence-backed minimal domain documentation is proposed or persisted; directory structure alone does not create multiple contexts, empty glossaries, or placeholder ADRs.
